content:
I had recently started formalizing some Jewish text in lean, and I think maybe more can be formalized potentially (in a Spinoza style).

Does anyone have any advice on how the right way to go about this is?
I think for this project to really take of a community is needed, so if anyone finds this idea interesting help me bug the maintainers to open a dedicated channel ;)
This is amusing, but what exactly is "formalising Jewish text"?
Something like this https://github.com/Nakammura/spinoza-ethica-lean

First of all, what do you mean by "help you bug the maintainers"? As @Patrick Massot already told you, it's unclear whether such a dedicated channel is needed. It is very much likely that until the community interested in this grow significantly, a thread will be enough: why do you think it won't, @Aryeh Shebson ?

Secondly, upon checking your first files, I realise that you redefine quite a bit of "fundamental" results, concerning addition on the naturals, for example. Can you disclose if AI has been used, and how, in your project? This does not seem to be clarified in your reamde.md
Just making a joke, a thread may be enough, but a channel adds legitimacy
AI was used quite a bit, my project is more of a proof of concept then something polished

Finally: there is virtual no reference in your text, neither to specific portions of the Mishnah nor to precise commentaries; and you should add a lot of docstrings: for example, why do you want that designationConflict defaults to false (the boolean, btw, and not the Prop False?
The project is just a formalization of Rabbi Moshe Koppel’s work as I stated in the README I think
I take this criticism to mean you may be interested in the idea?

Aryeh Shebson said:

Just making a joke, a thread may be enough, but a channel adds legitimacy

So it's better to wait until his legitimacy is obtained. To start off, it would help if you can declare this AI use in details in your readme, together with your aims and goals for the project.

Aryeh Shebson said:

I take this criticism to mean you may be interested in the idea?

I'm interested in Jewish texts, and I am personally interested in a carefully crafted formalisation of some of their notions. But this does not mean that, as a project, is suitable for this community and this Zulip, where several criteria need to be met. I urge you to read them in detail before moving forward.
That’s fair, where do you think the appropriate location should be? I just thought this Zulip is for any interesting projects written in lean

Well, this Zulip is for people ready to join a community that obeys to several strict rules: these are needed to make this space useful for people actively, and often profesionally, working on lean-related projects. Most of us are computer scientists and mathematicians, which does not mean that these criteria are mandatory, but showing up just saying "I've asked Claude to develop a fun project for me on ***, please have a look" is not in scope. For this, you can use general social networks, if you wish. Once more, if you think you're serious about this project, please do read the guidelines linked above and abide to them; if not, which is perfectly fine, just develop your project on your own.
sorry if I broke the rules, my only intention was to start a conversation, if this is inappropriate, please close this thread

Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

I've asked Claude to develop a fun project for me on ***, please have a look

Where has anything like that been said? Am I missing context?

Where is the repo link, even? I only see the link to that spinoza-ethica-lean repo.

As far as I can see in this thread, Aryeh was just trying to see if anyone would be interested in such a project.

I think there's some confusion in this thread whether

Aryeh Shebson said:

Something like this https://github.com/Nakammura/spinoza-ethica-lean

is @Aryeh Shebson's project or just an example of something similar for reference. Could you clarify?
yeah, just an example, project is by a guy named Nakammura
@Arthur Paulino the reason why this conversation is non-trivial to follow is it is split between two threads. See #Zulip meta > Request: formalizing Jewish texts channel
In particular the other thread does contain a link to https://github.com/ashebson/kinin-lean

Yes, thanks for clarifying. Regardless, we have a channel #AI authored projects, perhaps it would be better to zulip-move the conversation there, where people who are not interested in AI formalization can safely ignore it?
fair, not trying to break any rules here, just start an interesting conversation
then again, the discussion I am looking to starts isn't around my repo, my repo is only an example people can ignore
would love a ruling from whoever's authority it is to give one
You can click on names to see Filippo, Chris and I are all administrators of this Zulip instance.
so would it be ok to have this conversation under AI authored projects? somewhere else? or is the zulip inappropriate all together?

That's nuanced, because someone might as well be interested in the topic regardless of whether AI is used or not. I'm just unsure whether this Zulip community is the right audience for such a discussion.
